finding: Self-report and HbA1c are two different instruments with moderate-to-substantial agreement
decision: Use the union L_comb as training target; report PA/NA next to kappa; keep L_self and L_A1c as sensitivity labels SL2/SL1
alternatives_rejected: Single-instrument label (L_self or L_A1c) as target; kappa alone (prevalence-dependent)
check_note: Confusion table, kappa, PA/NA, sens/PPV recomputed and asserted against process doc §8

finding: Treatment masks diabetes in HbA1c: an HbA1c-only label turns controlled patients into negatives
evidence_value: 250/819 (30.5%) self-reported diabetics have HbA1c<6.5; 165 of them on medication; 23.8% of treated patients below 6.5
decision: Reject L_A1c as the sole target; keep stratum D_controlled as a 3x3 evaluation column; medication is audit-only (post-diagnosis)
alternatives_rejected: HbA1c-only target; medication as a feature (leakage by the availability rule)

finding: Most undiagnosed adults had contact with the health system: the gap is diagnosis/communication, not only access
evidence_value: of 152 undiagnosed: 36 told borderline (24%), 104 blood-tested in past 3 y (68%), 48 told prediabetes
decision: Frame E-SCREEN positives as 'not diagnosed despite contact'; DIQ160/DIQ180 excluded as features (post-test information); borderline kept negative in L_comb and flagged
alternatives_rejected: Describe undiagnosed as 'no access to care'; use DIQ180 as a screening feature
